newsitem.title: USA: Norwest sees Q1 as mirror for rest of '97.
newsitem.headline: Norwest sees Q1 as mirror for rest of '97.

text.p: Norwest Corp chief executive officer Richard Kovacevich said 1997 results are likely to mirror first-quarter results for the financial services company.

"If you look at the pattern in the first quarter, that's a pretty good indicator of what 1997 is likely to be like, where we had robust non-interest revenue growth, good interest revenue growth and some much-improved efficiencies," Kovacevich said Tuesday.
In the first quarter, Norwest's non-interest revenue increased 25 percent to $690.6 million and interest revenue revenue increased 5.5 percent to $1.61 billion.
At the shareholders' annual meeting, Kovacevich cited an improvement in Norwest's efficiency ratio to 63 percent in the first quarter of 1997. Back in 1992, it was 72 percent.

After the meeting, Kovacevich told reporters that continued improvement in the company's efficiency ratio would come over a number of years. "The pace (of improvement in the efficiency ratio) is OK. But we need to get into the 50s in the next few years. Mix has a lot to to with the efficiency ratio. We are heavily into fee-based businesses that tend to have higher efficiency ratios than banking," he said.
Efficiency ratio is defined as non-interest expense expressed as a percentage of the sum of net interest revenues and non-interest revenues.
